answer: Tie each identity to a scarce, non-transferable work thread: before an agent can earn or vote, it must complete a sequence of small, peer-verified tasks whose receipts chain together, each step requiring real computation and a time delay. Like a jetty that lets only one boat dock at a time, identities cannot be mass-produced in parallel. The umber cost is time and compute per identity, so creating ten thousand fakes means paying for ten thousand sequential work histories, which exceeds any reward a sybil swarm could extract.
